content.title: About
content.content: Rye bread is a whole‑grain loaf made from rye flour, water, yeast (or sourdough starter) and salt. It has a dense crumb, a slightly sour taste and a dark colour. Rye bread is a staple in many Northern and Eastern European cuisines.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Rye bread is often called “black bread”, although its shade varies with the rye variety and flour roasting level.
The sourdough starter used in rye bread contains lactic‑acid bacteria that enhance flavour and extend shelf life.
Rye flour provides more fiber and minerals than wheat flour, making the bread more nutritious.
In Russia and Poland rye bread is considered a national food and is commonly served with soups and borscht.
There are many regional versions, from very dense “black” loaves to lighter “half‑rye” breads.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety and helps regulate blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Rye bread supplies thiamine, niacin and folate, which are important for energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It contains magnesium, phosphorus, iron and zinc, essential for bones, blood and immunity.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Compared with white wheat bread, rye bread raises blood glucose more slowly, which is beneficial for people with pre‑diabetes.

items.title: Supports gut microbiota
items.content: The sourdough starter provides probiotic bacteria that may promote a healthy intestinal flora.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Rye bread contains gluten and is unsuitable for individuals with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High salt content
items.content: Some rye breads are heavily salted; people with hypertension should choose low‑salt varieties.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Because of the sourdough, the bread can be more acidic, which may cause discomfort for those with gastritis.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Rye bread works well for sandwiches, toast, and as a side for soups and salads. It can be toasted, spread with butter, cottage cheese, avocado, or used as a base for croutons.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the loaf in a paper bag or cloth sack at room temperature to keep the crust crisp. For longer storage keep it in an airtight container in the refrigerator (up to 1 week) or freeze (up to 3 months).

content.title: About
content.content: Coconut water is the clear liquid found inside a young green coconut. This product contains no added sugar, preserving its natural light sweetness and mineral-rich profile.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Coconut water naturally contains electrolytes such as potassium, sodium, magnesium, and calcium.
Unlike coconut milk, coconut water is virtually fat‑free.
Traditionally it has been consumed in tropical regions as a natural post‑exercise hydration drink.
Fresh coconut water typically contains 2–3 g of sugar per 100 ml, but the unsweetened version adds no extra sugar.
It can be used as a base for smoothies, marinades, and desserts.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: A rich electrolyte profile helps replenish fluids lost through sweat and supports overall water balance.

items.title: Low calorie content
items.content: Unsweetened coconut water provides about 20 kcal per 100 ml, making it a light beverage for weight management.

items.title: Heart support
items.content: Potassium contributes to normal blood pressure and promotes healthy heart function.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Contains vitamin C and small amounts of phenolic compounds that combat free radicals.

items.title: Digestive aid
items.content: A modest amount of dietary fiber helps maintain regular bowel movements.

items.title: Coconut allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to coconut water.

items.title: High potassium levels
items.content: People with kidney disease or on potassium‑affecting medications should limit intake.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Although low, excessive consumption could be a concern for those on strict sodium-restricted diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drink it chilled as a refreshing beverage, blend it into smoothies, use it in cocktails, marinate meats, or as a light base for desserts. It can also be gently warmed for hot drinks.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the bottle refrigerated after opening. Once opened, it is best consumed within 3–5 days. Avoid storing above 25 °C to prevent spoilage.

content.title: About
content.content: Dried Fruit NFS is an assortment of various fruits dried at low temperature without added sugar or preservatives. The drying process retains most of the vitamins, minerals, and natural flavor, making the product convenient for long‑term storage and transport.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Dried fruits are used in traditional dishes worldwide, from Mediterranean salads to Asian desserts.
Drying reduces the weight of the fruit by 5–7 times, facilitating shipping and storage.
Unlike sweetened dried fruits, NFS varieties keep the fruit’s natural sweetness.
They are a good source of dietary fiber, which supports digestion.
Proper drying preserves antioxidants such as polyphenols that are present in fresh fruit.

items.title: Rich in vitamins
items.content: Dried fruits contain B‑vitamins, small amounts of vitamin C, and vitamin A, which help maintain immunity and vision.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: They provide potassium, magnesium, and iron, essential for normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: High dietary fiber content promotes intestinal motility and contributes to a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: Dried fruits deliver quick‑acting carbohydrates, useful for athletes and anyone needing rapid energy.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Polyphenols and carotenoids are retained, helping to combat free radicals.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Although no sugar is added, natural sugars can be high, which should be considered by people with diabetes.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Dried fruits are calorie‑dense, so portion sizes should be moderate.

items.title: Sulfites
items.content: Some producers use sulfites to preserve color; they may cause allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: Small pieces can pose a choking risk for young children.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Dried fruits can be enjoyed as a snack, added to granola, yogurt, baked goods, salads, or used in sauces and marinades. They can also be re‑hydrated in water or juice to restore softness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dried fruits in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For extended storage, keep them in the refrigerator to prevent mold growth and flavor degradation.

content.title: About
content.content: Grilled trout is a tender fish with a distinctive smoky aroma. Cooking it over an open flame retains all of its nutritional benefits while the skin becomes crisp and the flesh stays juicy and flavorful.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Trout belongs to the salmon family and is commonly farmed in freshwater ponds.
Its omega‑3 fatty acid content is higher than that of most marine fish.
Traditionally, trout is grilled over open fires in Alpine regions, where it is considered a delicacy.
Several species exist, including rainbow, golden, and brown trout.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3
items.content: Omega‑3 fatty acids support heart health, improve vascular function, and reduce inflammation.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Trout provides easily digestible protein that aids muscle growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains B12, B6, and niacin, which are essential for metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Trout is a good source of selenium, phosphorus, and potassium, supporting immunity and electrolyte balance.

items.title: Low mercury
items.content: Compared with many ocean fish, trout typically has minimal mercury levels.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to fish, including trout.

items.title: Parasite contamination
items.content: Raw or undercooked trout can harbor parasites; ensure it is cooked thoroughly.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: When seasoned with salt or marinades, sodium levels can rise, which may be a concern for hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve grilled trout hot, often with lemon, herbs, or a light sauce. It can be enjoyed as fillet or with the skin on. Pairs well with roasted vegetables, potatoes, or whole‑grain grains.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked trout in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze it in air‑tight bags where it retains quality for up to 3 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of at least 63 °C before serving.

content.title: About
content.content: Tapioca pudding is a dessert made from a dry mix of tapioca pearls, sugar and flavorings. When hot water or milk is added, the mixture quickly thickens into a smooth, slightly gelatinous pudding with a mild, sweet taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tapioca is derived from the root of the cassava plant, cultivated in tropical regions of Asia, Africa and South America.
Dry mixes allow the pudding to be ready in 5–10 minutes without pre‑soaking the pearls.
Tapioca is gluten‑free, making it suitable for gluten‑free diets.
Its high starch content makes it an excellent thickener for soups and sauces.
Traditional Thai dessert “tapioca with coconut milk” uses the same basic ingredients.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Tapioca provides quickly digestible carbohydrates that give a rapid energy boost.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: The starch in tapioca is gentle on the stomach, suitable for people with sensitive digestion.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Absence of gluten makes it safe for individuals with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Tapioca contains virtually no fat, allowing it to be used in low‑calorie desserts.

items.title: Contains trace minerals
items.content: Enriched mixes may include small amounts of calcium and iron.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Tapioca can raise blood sugar quickly, so people with diabetes should consume it in moderation.

items.title: Cassava allergy
items.content: Rarely, individuals may be allergic to cassava, experiencing skin rash or swelling.

items.title: Excess starch
items.content: Large portions may cause bloating or discomfort in those with sensitive digestion.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pour hot water or milk over the dry mix, stir thoroughly and let it sit for 3–5 minutes. Serve the pudding warm or chilled, topped with fresh fruit, berries, nuts or a sprinkle of cinnamon.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the dry mix in a sealed container in a cool, dry place away from moisture and direct sunlight. Once opened, use within 3–4 months.
